prompt: Match each persistence setting or command to its durability effect.
explanation: The fsync policy sets the per-crash loss window for the AOF; save points drive RDB snapshot frequency; and BGREWRITEAOF compacts the log. Riskier policies are faster: no lets the OS decide, everysec risks about one second, and always risks nothing but costs the most latency.

pairs.right: Fsyncs after every write: strongest durability, highest latency
Fsyncs about once per second: roughly one second of writes at risk
The OS decides when to flush: fastest, least predictable loss window
RDB snapshot after 900 seconds if at least one key changed
Compacts the AOF into a minimal equivalent log in the background
